Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
- What the test asserts:
  - winzipBackSlashWorkaround() reads the 3rd entry from a WinZip-created archive and asserts the entry name equals "ä/". This implies two things must be true when reading:
    - The umlaut ä must decode correctly.
    - A directory entry must use a forward slash (/) as the trailing separator.

- How ZipArchiveInputStream currently reads names:
  - In ZipArchiveInputStream.getNextZipEntry():
    - It parses the general purpose bit and, if the UTF-8 flag is set, uses UTF-8 to decode the entry name (lines ~196–205, ~226–236).
      - hasUTF8Flag = gpFlag.usesUTF8ForNames()
      - entryEncoding = UTF8 if hasUTF8Flag else the configured zipEncoding
    - It then decodes the raw fileName bytes with entryEncoding and sets the name verbatim:
      - current.entry.setName(entryEncoding.decode(fileName), fileName) (line ~235)
    - There is no normalization step to replace backslashes with forward slashes.

- How directory detection works:
  - ZipArchiveEntry.isDirectory() returns getName().endsWith("/") (lines ~502–505).
  - If a name ends with a backslash "\" (as created by some WinZip versions on Windows), isDirectory() will return false.

- Why this fails for WinZip + umlauts:
  - WinZip on Windows may store directory names with backslashes as separators and a trailing "\".
  - In this test archive, the directory name is “ä\” in the raw LFH file name.
  - The code correctly decodes the umlaut ä because the UTF-8 flag is set, but it preserves the trailing backslash because no normalization occurs.
  - Therefore, the entry’s name becomes "ä\" rather than "ä/", and isDirectory() doesn’t recognize it as a directory (and the test’s assertEquals("\u00e4/", zae.getName()) fails).

- Evidence in code:
  - Name decoding and setting happens without any path separator fix: current.entry.setName(entryEncoding.decode(fileName), fileName).
  - No use of versionMadeBy/platform to normalize separators even though current.entry.setPlatform(...) is set earlier (lines ~191–195).
  - isDirectory() strictly checks '/'.

- Root cause:
  - Missing normalization of Windows-style backslashes to forward slashes when reading entry names from the local file header. This omission makes WinZip-created directory entries (with trailing '\') not match expected forward-slash format and not be recognized as directories.

- Conclusion:
  - The failure occurs because ZipArchiveInputStream.getNextZipEntry() sets the entry name directly from the decoded bytes without converting backslashes to forward slashes. This causes "ä\" to be returned instead of the expected "ä/", breaking both the name assertion and directory recognition.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
